hypotheses: Observed Goose tail regression affects all endpoint families during a shared transient, so it cannot be attributed solely to direct login latency. A shared database, scheduler, or queue interaction is plausible.

Goose uses more PostgreSQL CPU and twice as many persistent client backends; combined target/client CPU approaches the shared 10-logical-CPU VM during the burst. Scheduling pressure and client wake lag can amplify a database or writer stall.
An additional PostgreSQL PID appears after burst onset and recurs 60 seconds later. Its process role was not recorded; autovacuum or another background worker is a hypothesis, not a proven cause.

There are no recorded per-request server queue times, query traces, PostgreSQL wait events or fsync counters here. These data cannot distinguish writer commit stalls from specific SQL/backend or per-loop queue stalls.
